races.name: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle on Saturday, August 29th Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Boston Common
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse in a race where the rear is already overcrowded — drawn into a midfield slot on the map but will likely settle at the back as instinct takes over; the fading-in-finish flag and a modest recent form string of UP62/0 make a winning intervention hard to envisage.

runners_data.name: Casper Charlie
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has shown ability on Good ground over similar trips but carries a fade flag and a form string of just 0-F — Phillip Enright's experience gives him a positional edge, though the question is whether this horse can see out the 2m4f trip without tying up.

runners_data.name: Coral Reid
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity with no publicly visible form or going preference — Tom Kelly takes the 7lb claim but the lightly-raced flag and UNKNOWN going profile mean this runner must be treated with maximum caution.

runners_data.name: Goodmancon
runners_data.note: Consistent placer who has finished second or third on five of eleven visible runs, but his natural rear-of-field style will be squeezed in this large field and he arrives here having missed the frame last time; the 33-day break is neutral, but counting on him to travel from the back in a slowly-run race is a stretch.

runners_data.name: Installment
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes the ride on a horse last seen just 11 days ago, and the trainer's 1/5 14-day record suggests the yard is trying — however, this is a genuine hold-up type slotted into a midfield position it may never realistically occupy, and a form line of /67-4P over Good provides modest encouragement.

runners_data.name: Minella Moon Shine
runners_data.note: Second on his only visible start at 2m, handled Good ground and arrives 29 days fresh under Daniel King for a yard in 1/1 form; his prominent style is ideally suited to the race shape if he can track the leader and produce a clean round.

runners_data.name: Rodeo Joe
runners_data.note: 389 days off the track is an enormous absence for a horse with a form string of PPP/P- — Paddy Cody on the 7lb claim cannot compensate for the rustiness, and this runner is a dangerous one to include in any scenario involving the front group.

runners_data.name: Ruled By The Sun
runners_data.note: Moderate form — two sevens and a P in recent starts — and the tongue strap is noted; two runs in 11 days hints at a trainer trying to find the right surface but the Going: OK tag and consistent inability to place make this a long shot.

runners_data.name: Seven Towers
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's consistent performer has placed third or better on four of his last six runs on Good or similar ground, and Keith Donoghue's positional awareness suits the prominent role — the only negative is a career absence of a win, suggesting a horse that finds one better late on.

runners_data.name: Who's Going
runners_data.note: 122 days off for Gordon Elliott's four-year-old, with a career-best form string showing 0, 8 and finishing tailed-off last time on Soft — the stable is in form (2/43 at 14 days) but this is the shortest and most unexposed runner in the field, and the fade flag is a significant concern.

runners_data.name: Cool Native
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy aboard is the biggest positive here — an experienced partnership, two recent thirds on Good over similar distances, and a horse that jumps well and travels prominently; the tongue strap and OR of 109 (lowest in field) raise a weight-in-class question, but the form is honest and the positional profile fits the likely race shape well.

runners_data.name: Louve d'Arc
runners_data.note: 140 days off the track for William Harvey's five-year-old who finished eighth last time on Good; the long absence and modest placed form make this hard to enthuse about despite the Good-ground tag.

runners_data.name: Maple Mornin
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner who will lead from flag to flag at a pace of his own choosing — the fade flag is a genuine concern over 2m4f, and Eoin Staples (5lb claim) is relatively unexposed; the race revolves around how honest and sustainable this horse's lead will be.

runners_data.name: Star Cave
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with a ⚠ flag but shows a fourth over the same 2m4f trip on Good — Simon Torrens rides for a yard with 0/3 at 14 days, and the unknown going qualifier combined with a single data point means this runner is a genuine question mark with some residual interest on trip.

runners_data.name: Tumbling In
runners_data.note: Four consecutive thirds on Good ground — the most consistent placing record in the field — and arrives 18 days fresh for a yard that is 0/5 in the 14-day window; the 2m4f trip is beyond anything in his visible history but the consistent jumping and finish suggests he stays further than 2m.

runners_data.name: Xquise
runners_data.note: 594 days off the track is the longest absence in the field and an almost impossible barrier to overcome — flat form on the Strand course bears no relevance to a 2m4f hurdle, and the fade flag seals a deeply negative assessment.

runners_data.name: Carrigane
runners_data.note: 50-day break for a horse that finished fourth on his only visible Good-ground run — a natural hold-up type who will not get the midfield position shown on the map in a 19-runner field, and without a jockey named in the data this entry carries additional uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Kalico Leader
runners_data.note: Unknown going profile and lightly raced flag with the most recent form showing a second — Edward Buckley's yard is 1/3 at 14 days which is a mild positive, but the absence of a jockey and the 92-day gap make this a genuine wildcard.

runners_data.name: Siege Of Milan
runners_data.note: No form, no going data, no jockey listed and an LR of blank days — Ross O'Sullivan fields consistent performers but there is simply no evidence here on which to base any assessment, making this the most opaque runner in the race.

races.paceDynamic: Maple Mornin is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 19 and will set off in front unchallenged, dictating a sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m4f at Roscommon. With no genuine rival willing or able to press early, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which compresses the advantage for late finishers and makes positional comfort off a slow-burn tempo the key asset. Minella Moon Shine, Seven Towers, Casper Charlie and Cool Native are the most likely horses to sit in the prominent group just behind, and in a one-pace scenario they will be best placed to pounce. Several runners — Installment, Goodmancon, Carrigane and Boston Common — are genuinely hold-up types pushed forward on the map because the rear is over-subscribed; they are unlikely to secure those midfield berths naturally and should be treated as true rearward runners. The race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield types who can travel handy and sustain their effort through the final climb, rather than true closers who will find the pace insufficient to generate the gaps they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Maple Mornin Leads, Prominents Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Maple Mornin sets a controlled gallop and the prominents travel comfortably throughout.
scenarios.body: Maple Mornin bowls along at a measured clip, and the horses sitting just behind — Seven Towers, Cool Native and Minella Moon Shine — travel within themselves before asserting from 2 out; the steady tempo rewards those with tactical speed and hurdles experience over the distance. Hold-up horses are left with too little to aim at in the straight and the winner comes from the first four or five jumping the final flight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Dries Up, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Maple Mornin's gallop is truly dawdling and Minella Moon Shine or Seven Towers move to press before the home turn.
scenarios.body: A tactical crawl turns the race into a sprint from 3 out, and any horse who has the acceleration and jumping fluency to go early gets first run on the field; Seven Towers' consistent placing record and Minella Moon Shine's recent second suggest they have the cruising speed for this shape. The hold-up brigade, despite their redistribution, simply cannot generate enough momentum from the rear to reel in a front pair who kick early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: True Hold-Ups Weave Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and creates a genuine test that frees up the track for late finishers.
scenarios.body: Should a secondary mover — perhaps Casper Charlie or a prominent horse making a mistake — inject more pace mid-race, the closing stretch could open up for runners like Tumbling In or Goodmancon who have consistent placed form in similar distances on Good ground. This scenario depends on the true hold-up types getting clear runs, which in a 19-runner field on a sharp track is far from guaranteed, keeping the probability low.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Large Field
scenarios.trigger: If the large 19-runner field causes crowding, interference or a melee at hurdles.
scenarios.body: With 19 runners over fences and bends at Roscommon, fallers or interference could scramble the order and deliver a random result from an unlikely position; horses that are handy and robust jumpers would survive best. This scenario is a low-probability lottery — named here for completeness — with Cool Native's jumping profile making him the most likely beneficiary if the field strings out chaotically.

watchPoints.text: Maple Mornin carries a fade flag over 2m4f — if this sole front-runner ties up approaching the last, the entire front group could be swallowed simultaneously and reshuffle every scenario.

The 19-runner field creates significant jumping risk at the early hurdles on Roscommon's tight track — watch for crowding and interference in the first half-mile involving the hold-up group (Installment, Goodmancon, Carrigane) who will be fighting for position they cannot naturally secure.

Cool Native and Seven Towers are both prominent types for the same ground and trip — if they clash for position directly behind Maple Mornin, one will be forced wider or back, altering the complexion of the race for Scenarios A and B.

Xquise (594 days), Rodeo Joe (389 days) and Who's Going (122 days) represent a trio of long-absentees whose race fitness is unverifiable — monitor market moves at post time for any sign of stable confidence, as each could be a drifter or a springer.

Tumbling In's four consecutive thirds suggest a horse that consistently finds one or two better — watch whether the step up to 2m4f finally allows him to sustain his effort to the line or whether the extra distance exposes a stamina ceiling.

races.name: James Lohan Engineering Excellence Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Clay Pigeons
runners_data.note: Mullins/Hayes combination commands respect — won at 19f on Good and 16f on Soft, proven at this trip and a strong prominent profile who should travel smoothly just off a hot pace; 198 days off the track is a minor query but Mullins horses rarely need race fitness.|

runners_data.name: Minella Hollow
runners_data.note: Won twice on Good ground over 16f with John Nallen, style suits prominent tracking; 289-day absence is a significant flag and the step up to 1m7½f is new ground, but two victories on similar going gives confidence if fit enough.|

runners_data.name: Earthwatch
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type from Denis Hogan's yard, four recent 4th-place finishes on Good ground suggest reliability without a finishing flourish; only 11 days since last run and the 4yo has shown a capacity to stay the trip — look for the late run only if pace is truly terminal.|

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator whose recent form is over shorter (flat) and who switches codes here; the hg:p headgear note and 8-day turnaround from Paul Flynn's yard are both worth noting, but the lack of any obvious jumping form and modest going record (0W) leave plenty to prove.|

runners_data.name: Haughty
runners_data.note: Amateur rider (Mr B M Coonan 7lb claim), and recent runs of PP on hurdles suggest jumping issues rather than ability concerns; form over shorter on Standard and Soft ground doesn't obviously translate to 1m7½f Good, making this a very speculative each-way vehicle at best.|

runners_data.name: Captain Hanley
runners_data.note: Showed two solid placed runs over 20-24f on Good, a genuine stamina-loving hold-up type in nature — however, with the field loaded with forward-going horses he is unlikely to find clear daylight from the rear and his race chance is tempered by the inability to fulfil his natural role here.|

runners_data.name: Chantilly Wings
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who shapes as the most likely to steal a march if the pace battle thins the other speedsters — recent 2nd on Good and consistent finishes across Good ground make this the pace horse with the best form credentials; Carl Millar's 5lb claim is a mild positive.|

runners_data.name: Kilmond Knight
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish, with only two hurdles runs on record and a recent P-U0 string suggesting problems completing; Alan O'Sullivan's claim can't offset the obvious stamina/jumping doubts at 1m7½f in a large, quick field.|

runners_data.name: Le Roi Arthur
runners_data.note: 318-day layoff is a major concern for a confirmed front-runner whose most recent form shows a 9th and a 3rd over shorter; Edward Buckley's 1/3 T14 record is modest and a horse this fresh going straight to the front in a three-way pace battle is a risky proposition.|

runners_data.name: Saviour Blu
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in the finish and a 0W0P record in three starts on Good, the hg:h headgear note and recent 0-U0 form make this one of the least appealing profiles in the race — prominent mapping but little evidence of staying power at 1m7½f.|

runners_data.name: Whoyougonnacall
runners_data.note: Recent 3rd over 18f on Good is encouraging, and a prominent/midfield profile suits when the pace truly collapses; Michael Kenneally's claim (5lb) for the John Patrick Ryan yard (1/19 T14) is modest but if the race falls apart up front this one has the staying form to capitalise.|

runners_data.name: Direct Approach
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy's booking for Gordon Elliott (2/43 T14) is the standout note here — a hold-up horse whose 3rd over 19f on Good last time is directly relevant, and the top jockey/trainer combination in a 19-runner field gives it a significant edge if late closers get their day.|

runners_data.name: Glenmore Graduate
runners_data.note: J J Slevin is a strong booking but the horse carries lightly-raced and fades-in-finish flags, and recent form of 11th and 9th over long trips on Good suggest it hasn't found its level yet; Peter Maher's yard carries no T14 activity which limits confidence.|

runners_data.name: Leva Deva
runners_data.note: Two runs, both over 18f on Good, both resulting in 14th and a pulled-up, with the fades-in-finish flag attached — 56-day absence doesn't obviously revive prospects, and this shape (hot pace, stamina test) does nothing to flatter a horse without a placed run to its name.|

runners_data.name: Prophetess Miriam
runners_data.note: Two previous 2nd-place finishes on Good ground over 16f with the hg:h note suggest a genuine each-way profile — a prominent/midfield style in the hands of Eoin Walsh for Cian Collins' yard (who also saddle Chantilly Wings) and Good ground at an extended trip suits.|

runners_data.name: Speisialta
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner but recent form of 4-R0 and a hg:h note are worrying — 12 days since last run and a history of non-completions raises the question of whether it can even stay the trip at this pace; if it leads, it may capitulate well before the last.|

runners_data.name: Ataboymiley
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell's runner is unknown on going with no public form showing, lightly raced flag attached — a total unknown quantity whose chance depends entirely on how much the trainer has gleaned at home; impossible to assess positively.|

runners_data.name: John Gun
runners_data.note: A 4yo from Kieran Purcell's yard with no LR date or going record — another complete unknown in a large field where experienced runners hold a clear edge; the lightly-raced flag is critical at this distance on a testing Good surface.|

runners_data.name: Goeasyonme
runners_data.note: John Patrick Ryan's second runner alongside Whoyougonnacall, also unknown on going and lightly raced — no data to work from, which in a 19-runner maiden hurdle over nearly two miles makes this extremely difficult to assess; trainer's yard has 1/19 T14 which is slim evidence at best.|

races.paceDynamic: Speisialta, Le Roi Arthur, and Chantilly Wings are all confirmed front-runners in a 19-runner maiden hurdle over 1m7½f on Good ground at Roscommon, making a strong early gallop virtually certain with three horses likely competing for the lead from the outset. That contest for supremacy will stretch the field early, burning off stamina reserves and ensuring this race is run at a searching, unrelenting tempo throughout. Clay Pigeons and Minella Hollow are the class prominent types best positioned to travel in behind the pace, while genuine hold-up operators like Direct Approach and Whoyougonnacall will have the strongest closing legs if the pace duly collapses the front-runners. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield racers with proven stamina and the tactical nous to sit just off a hot pace — horses who won't over-exert early but have the engine to pick up the pieces when the pace-setters cry enough. The field holds more hold-up types than can all secure their natural rear position; Captain Hanley, a genuine back-of-the-field operator, has been redistributed to a midfield mapping, but in practice will likely struggle to settle into that role with so many runners going forward and may forfeit any positional advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners tear into the race and burn each other out, leaving the prominent runners to take command from the home turn.
scenarios.body: The relentless early gallop set by Speisialta, Le Roi Arthur, and Chantilly Wings will leave attrition in their wake, and horses tracking just behind the speed with stamina intact will be perfectly placed to inherit the prize from two out. Clay Pigeons (Mullins/Hayes, proven at this trip on Good ground) and Minella Hollow (two wins in going similar) hold the class and stamina profile to exploit this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly suicidal and the front three completely implode, enabling genuine hold-up horses to sweep past a strung-out field in the final flight.
scenarios.body: A hot pace on Good ground over nearly two miles can absolutely cook the principals, and horses ridden for a late run will have clear daylight to sprint at a tiring field from the last. Direct Approach (Jack Kennedy booking is significant, 3rd last time), Earthwatch (consistent 4th-place finisher who stays) and Whoyougonnacall are the true closers best suited if this scenario fully materialises.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three pace horses — most likely Chantilly Wings or Le Roi Arthur — breaks clear of the early speed battle and controls a sustainable gallop alone.
scenarios.body: In this shape, one front-runner separates from the others early, settles into a rhythm and retains enough energy to kick again from two out while rivals are still scrapping through midfield. Chantilly Wings has the most consistent recent form of the lead trio and twice finished placed in Good ground handicaps at this distance band, giving it the best credentials to survive if it can steal the initiative.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Outsider Scores
scenarios.trigger: If the large field produces interference, fallers, or widespread traffic issues that shuffle the order dramatically and allow an unconsidered runner to emerge.
scenarios.body: A 19-runner jumps maiden over undulating Roscommon hurdles carries genuine risk of incident, and with the pace battle likely creating a compressed midfield, horse-related chaos could scramble normal finishing positions entirely. Glenmore Graduate (J J Slevin, Maher yard) or one of the unknown-going debutants (Ataboymiley, Goeasyonme) could emerge in a truly scrambled finish.

watchPoints.text: Three front-runners (Speisialta, Le Roi Arthur, Chantilly Wings) contesting the lead from the outset in a 19-runner field creates a high risk of interference and potential fallers at early hurdles — watch for the pace battle triggering a messy incident that reshapes the whole race.

Speisialta's hg:h headgear, R (refused) in recent form, and 12-day turnaround combine to make it an unpredictable leader — if it stops abruptly or refuses mid-race it could bring down horses immediately behind it.

Direct Approach (Jack Kennedy/Gordon Elliott) is the most potent late-run profile in the field — if the tempo is genuinely brutal, watch for Kennedy to produce it from further back than expected and time a run to the last.

Clay Pigeons at 198 days off the track is a fitness question mark despite the Mullins/Hayes alliance — if it travels strongly early that concern evaporates, but any sign of laboured movement through the first mile is a red flag to discount its chance of staying on.

Minella Hollow's 289-day absence is the longest in the field among any horse with a realistic chance — monitor pre-race market moves; a significant gamble would suggest the Nallen yard has done the groundwork, while drift would confirm the long layoff is a genuine concern.|

races.name: DNG Ivan Connaughton Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Born Bright
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator with three wins on Good ground at 24f, ridden by the 5lb claimer James Smith for a small yard; 57 days off the track but proven at this sort of trip and going combination — best served by a strong pace that seldom materialises here.

runners_data.name: Mephisto
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has run 15 times on Good ground and found the frame only three times; only 6 days since last run which is worth noting, and his hold-up style leaves him dependent on a punishing pace he is unlikely to get in this shape.

runners_data.name: Kalanisi Flash
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter and sole front-runner in the field — wears tongue-strap and blinkers and has won on Good, but recent form shows a string of pulled-ups (PP); style fit note flags she is racing slightly out of natural role given the rating, and the weight of 19 runners gives scope for pressure to arrive earlier than expected.

runners_data.name: Sound Judgement
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy booked for a six-year-old trained by Gordon Elliott represents the class angle here — won over 24f on Good and placed at 22f, and his prominent racing style is ideally aligned with the race shape that is most likely to develop; lightly raced for age with clear upside.

runners_data.name: Starzov
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old returning from 352 days off the track, and the flag for finishing fade compounds the concern about that layoff; hold-up style requires a pace injection that is unlikely to come, and his recent record on Good ground contains no placed efforts.

runners_data.name: Mavetherave
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes the ride for the O'Connell yard — prominent racer who finished second over 22f on Good here most recently, giving him direct Roscommon course form; no wins from nine Good-ground starts but places regularly and the trip suits.

runners_data.name: Priory Park
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old last seen 108 days ago and has finished out of the first four in four of his last five; hold-up style and a going record that shows only one place from ten Good-ground starts makes him hard to enthuse about at this stage of his career.

runners_data.name: Getaway Charlie
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose natural ground at the rear of the field is congested by the size of the field — shown in midfield on the map but genuinely wants to come from off the pace; 7lb claimer up, and the style-fit discount applies given he is unlikely to find his natural spot in a 19-runner race.

runners_data.name: It's Not His Fault
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who fades in the finish and is mapped forward of his natural position because of the crowded hold-up group; only two placing efforts from four Good-ground runs and a 152-day absence add further caution — the fade flag is particularly relevant over 3m.

runners_data.name: Itsaworkinmaniam
runners_data.note: Returns from 296 days off the course, a serious absence to overcome; genuine hold-up type who is one of the horses pushed forward on the map by the congestion at the rear, wearing a tongue-strap, with a style-fit discount in play given he can't realistically get his preferred position.

runners_data.name: Mr Dibbs
runners_data.note: Recent winner over 26f on Good ground for Gavin Cromwell — wears blinkers and has two wins from 14 Good-ground starts; hold-up style and a solid course-trip profile mean he needs a strong gallop, but he arrives here in form and with an official rating that is workable.

runners_data.name: Western Model
runners_data.note: Won over 24f on Good ground most recently and has placed six times on that surface — Donagh Meyler rides; hold-up racer who arrives in form and whose stamina at the trip is well established, making him one of the more interesting closers if any pace develops.

runners_data.name: She'll Be Kept
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground 14 days ago for Brian McMahon — the in-form angle is real, but she is a true rear-of-field operator being shown in midfield on the map because the back group is overcrowded; Phillip Enright rides and the going presents no issue, though the style-fit discount limits expectation.

runners_data.name: Glitz And Glamour
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent racer for the McNamara yard, ridden by a 5lb claimer; has placed on Good ground over 24f and gets this sort of trip, but a record of 8-3-9-P-6 in recent starts suggests inconsistency that needs resolving.

runners_data.name: Sallap
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago — the very short turnaround is the dominant concern; has won twice on Good over 22f and the form figures show recent improvement, but the fade flag and the natural hold-up style being mapped forward due to congestion combine to temper enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Knocknagoran Lady
runners_data.note: Won twice in recent starts on Good ground and arrives with form — another hold-up type whose natural position at the rear is compromised by the size of the field, with the style-fit discount in play; Daniel King takes over in the saddle for the small Hughes yard.

runners_data.name: Wild Mandate
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win over 26f on Good ground in his recent history — no jockey listed which is worth noting administratively; the trainer McNiff yard has had no runners in 14 days and he ran just two days ago, making fitness a non-issue but freshness a mild query.

runners_data.name: Smackwater Jack
runners_data.note: Twelve-year-old veteran with two wins from eight Good-ground starts over 22-24f — placed in his last two, and prominent style means he can get a position off the pace without burning reserves; the age is a question mark but current form justifies inclusion in the mix.

runners_data.name: Its Not Over Yet
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer whose best runs over 24f on Good ground give him the trip credentials, but he is among the group of closers mapped forward of his true position by the congested rear; the McKiernan yard has had no winner in 14 days and he ran 29 days ago — one for the watch list rather than the shortlist.

races.paceDynamic: Kalanisi Flash is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field over 3m at Roscommon, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, she is set to control this at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground. Sound Judgement, Mavetherave, Glitz And Glamour, Smackwater Jack, and Wild Mandate will press forward into prominent positions, creating a compact early order but without the fierce pace injection that would burn Kalanisi Flash off the front. The field contains substantially more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Itsaworkinmaniam, It's Not His Fault, Getaway Charlie, She'll Be Kept, Sallap, Knocknagoran Lady, and Its Not Over Yet are all natural rear-of-field runners who are being mapped further forward than their true role simply because the back of the field is congested; of these, Getaway Charlie and Itsaworkinmaniam are the most likely to actually secure a mid-to-rear position with any comfort. A controlled gallop over a stamina trip on Good ground will compress the field through the final circuit and produce a truly-run staying test where tactical position from the prominent group counts — horses who can travel into the race from the top five or six and sustain their effort from the last flight are the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kalanisi Flash Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Kalanisi Flash dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent pack lacks the will to put her under pressure before the final climb.
scenarios.body: Kalanisi Flash sets every fraction from the front and the controlled tempo rewards those who have travelled into the race without burning reserves; horses racing prominently off the pace can quicken into the gaps from the second-last flight with fresh legs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to string the field out and a prominent racer picks it up from second or third jumping the last.
scenarios.body: Sound Judgement and Smackwater Jack both have the course form and prominent style to get to the leader's girth at the right moment, and on Good ground over 3m their stamina profiles suit a race that builds rather than explodes.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely strong enough to bring the field back to the closers in the straight.
scenarios.body: Born Bright and Western Model are the true hold-up horses with the best Good-ground form credentials in this field, and if the tempo burns enough fuel from the leaders they can finish powerfully; however, the likely controlled pace makes a sustained late rattle less probable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the field concertinas and a chaotic finish develops after jumping errors or falls disrupt the controlled order.
scenarios.body: In a 19-runner field over 3m with a mix of handicappers, scrimmaging late can benefit horses who have avoided trouble and kept their jumping fluent throughout; Mr Dibbs and Western Model, both recent winners on Good ground, carry the form to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Starzov returns from 352 days off the track with a fade-in-finish flag over 3m — monitor closely in the straight for signs of distress, as a tired horse over this trip in a 19-runner field creates jumping danger for those behind.

With 19 runners over 3m and a cluster of hold-up horses unable to find their natural position, scrimmaging and crowding at the early hurdles is a genuine risk — watch how Getaway Charlie, Itsaworkinmaniam, and Sallap are placed out of the gate.

Sallap ran just two days ago and carries a fade flag — connections may have a reason for the quick return but the short turnaround over 3m on Good ground should be tracked through the second circuit to see if the effort tells.

Kalanisi Flash's recent form string of pulled-ups (PP) raises a question about whether she will complete the course even if allowed to dictate — if she weakens before the last two flights the race shape changes entirely and closers like Born Bright and Western Model move into frame.

Jack Kennedy on Sound Judgement is the marquee jockey booking in the race — watch his position jumping the third-last, as Kennedy tends to travel into handicaps rather than commit early, and any move from him into the top two or three at that point is a significant race-reading signal.

races.paceDynamic: Impero, trained by Cian Collins and ridden by Jack Kennedy, is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner beginners' chase and will stride into the lead from the outset on Good ground at Roscommon over 2m½f. With no rival likely to seriously contest the front rank, Impero can dictate a controlled, sustainable tempo — the classic scenario for a front-runner to conserve energy through the early fences and build on the lead turning for home. The field holds more hold-up types than can genuinely occupy their natural positions: Orkneys Jack, Killeemore Lad, and Piccolo Player are all true rear-division horses redistributed into midfield on the map, meaning the race is unlikely to produce the sort of strong late rush that would typically undermine a front-runner. This race shape heavily favours prominent and front-running profiles — horses capable of travelling close to Impero or tracking him into the straight are best placed to pounce if he tires, while the genuine closers face a structural disadvantage racing out of their natural role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Impero Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Impero sets a comfortable gallop from the front and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap on the final circuit.
scenarios.body: Impero, untroubled in front on Good ground over a trip he has placed at before, conserves enough energy to repel challengers jumping the final two fences; Hashtag Pretender, the one runner with the prominent style to track and mount a genuine challenge, is best placed of the chasers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Impero sets a marginally stronger pace than ideal and Hashtag Pretender or Silent Selector tracks closely enough to wear him down from the last.
scenarios.body: A horse racing prominently just off Impero's shoulder is ideally placed to capitalise the moment the leader's jumping or stamina wavers; Hashtag Pretender's recent placing form at similar trips on Good ground fits this shape, and Silent Selector's lone win came over 20f on Good going suggesting he stays well.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final circuit, compressing the field and allowing a redistributed hold-up type to produce a late run.
scenarios.body: Killeemore Lad, who won and placed twice over 16-17f on Good ground and is a genuine hold-up horse placed in midfield here, would be the chief beneficiary if the compressed pace creates a sprint finish; Orkneys Jack placed at OR=120 level on Good going and could also pick up pieces if the front rank ties up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Jumping Errors
scenarios.trigger: If early jumping errors disrupt the order, eliminate Impero or Hashtag Pretender, and radically redistribute the contest.
scenarios.body: A beginners' chase carries inherent jumping risk across all runners, and any significant departure at a fence could hand the advantage to whichever horse is most fluently jumping on the day; Silent Selector, who won a handicap hurdle and has placed at this level, or Killeemore Lad, with a chase win already banked, could inherit an altered race.

watchPoints.text: Swing Time has been off the track for 273 days with zero wins or places on Good going — monitor his jumping in the early stages as a novice returning cold to fences, as an error could disrupt runners around him.

Killeemore Lad and Orkneys Jack are both genuine hold-up horses racing out of their natural role in midfield — watch whether either can engineer their preferred position early or whether they get trapped in traffic and lose their chance before the final circuit.

Hashtag Pretender fell on his most recent start and has been off 59 days; watch his jumping at the early fences closely, as any hesitancy could see him lose his prominent position and hand Impero an even more comfortable lead.

Impero's controlled front-running will set the race tempo — if Kennedy chooses to kick on down the back straight rather than conserve, watch for Hashtag Pretender and Silent Selector being caught flat-footed and unable to close the gap before the final two fences.

races.paceDynamic: Dunany Point is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-horse field and should lead from the outset on Good ground at Roscommon over 2m5½f, setting a measured, sustainable gallop without any genuine pace rival likely to push him into a faster tempo. With only King's Son and Ballyredinkingston as prominent-style horses to track him, the early order will be relatively settled, creating a true-run but not gruelling pace that rewards horses who travel smoothly in the first half of the race. The stacked hold-up brigade — including Run For The Border, Ladies Well, Island McCoo, Jouster, and Gaoithe Glory — will need to make sustained ground from off the pace on a track that does not overly flatter closers, meaning mid-to-late movers must have real ability to bridge the gap. This race shape strongly favours prominent or handily-placed types who travel close to a controlled pace, land in a position to challenge from three out, and have the jumping fluency to capitalise — horses who can race in the first half-dozen and pounce from three fences out will hold the key structural advantage. The field holds far more hold-up horses than the race map can genuinely accommodate at the rear; of the redistributed horses, Not So Serious, Another Challenge, and Backinabit are those most likely to attempt to secure a more forward position than their natural style suggests, though it remains unlikely all will succeed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dunany Point Controls, Prominent Types Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Dunany Point leads at a fair clip unchallenged and the race is set up for horses racing close to the pace from the outset.
scenarios.body: Dunany Point dictates a sustainable rhythm that compresses the field, and horses like King's Son and Full Noise who travel prominently arrive with matching reserves at the last two fences; the honest Good ground rewards fluent jumping and a forward position without the pace being quick enough to string the field out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Sweep Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If Dunany Point sets a genuinely quick early tempo that burns off the prominent horses and opens the race for closers arriving with a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: The pace proves more attritional than expected over 2m5½f, and horses like Run For The Border, Ladies Well, or Island McCoo — who have the class and Good-ground form to pick up rivals — reel in the weakening leaders from two out; their better RPR figures give them the edge in a truly-run race that becomes a stamina test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Dunany Point bowls along at a deceptively strong gallop and simply refuses to be caught, turning a controlling front-running display into an outright win.
scenarios.body: On Good ground at Roscommon over this staying trip, a front-runner who jumps well and settles can find a second wind up the straight; with the hold-up horses too far back and unable to produce a telling late burst, Dunany Point's prominent record in similar conditions gives him every chance of stealing it.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace falters dramatically and the whole race is run at a crawl before a sprint finish from two out.
scenarios.body: A bunched, muddling race with a tactical finish would theoretically suit genuine hold-up horses, but many of the closers here are redistributed types racing out of role, reducing confidence that true rear-runners can deliver; Gaoithe Glory or Charlie's Gift might get a slice of the action but the scenario is undermined by the quality and style inconsistency of the hold-up group.

watchPoints.text: Dunany Point sets the tempo alone — if he jumps well through the first circuit and dictates a comfortable gallop, he becomes a live threat to win outright rather than just set the table for others.

Run For The Border is the highest-rated horse in the field at OR 95 but must make sustained ground from a hold-up position; watch whether the pace is strong enough to set him alight from three out, as his class could overpower rivals if conditions fall right.

Ladies Well arrives as a recent winner on Good ground with an elite sim-going strike rate — monitor her position at the top of the home straight, as a horse with her profile who travels smoothly could quicken decisively from two out.

runners_data.name: Il Silenzio

runners_data.name: Sampoet

runners_data.name: Thewaybackhome

races.paceDynamic: Sampoet and Kilashee are the two confirmed front-runners in this 19-runner handicap chase over 3m1f, and with both likely to push forward from the off, this race will be run at an honest, contested gallop from the first fence — neither can be expected to dominate unchallenged. Thewaybackhome and Oogum Boogum are genuine prominent types who will press close to the pace, adding further compression to the early stages and ensuring the leaders are never fully allowed to coast. The field is loaded with hold-up horses — Stormy Master, Made U Look, True Harmony, Written In My Soul, Captain Kate, Deal Again and Love Like This are all natural rear-pacers who have been pushed into midfield on the map simply because there is no room for them all to settle where they want — meaning those runners will race partially out of their comfort zone and face a tougher task than their style would normally suggest. In a 3m1f Roscommon chase run at a genuine clip on Good ground, the race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel close to the pace without burning their petrol early, then pick off the leaders between the last two fences — the premium is on horses proven to travel well in the first half and finish off the trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Soften, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Sampoet and Kilashee push along as expected and drain enough energy from the pace that a well-positioned prominent mover picks up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Thewaybackhome and Oogum Boogum are ideally placed to stalk the leaders through the middle section and accelerate as the front two come back to the field from the third-last; both have consistent form at this level and suit the good ground. Difficult Decision has the course form and prominent profile to also benefit from a soft-ended pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Last Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is more moderate than expected — Kilashee especially fading — and one of the leaders steals a winning break from the front.
scenarios.body: Sampoet has solid good-ground form and if Kilashee weakens and drops away, Sampoet could dictate to himself from the halfway point at a more comfortable tempo and be first home; this is less likely with a competitive 19-runner field but his natural prominence means it cannot be ruled out. Ballagh Star, who has shown a winner's profile at big-field trips, would be best-placed of the prominent types to push on and steal from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Strong Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is truly severe and the front rank collapses late, giving the genuine hold-up horses — those not redistributed — a clear run home.
scenarios.body: Il Silenzio is the one authentic hold-up performer whose good-ground record at 25f+ trips (1W2P in good going) gives it the best credentials to finish strongly if the pace burns itself out; Kilkee Bay won last time out in soft and shapes to stay, and with good-ground form figures of 12/15 is not disadvantaged by the conditions. One Way Traffic is consistent enough to land in the frame from off the pace if stamina becomes the deciding factor.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early fractions cause widespread attrition among the favourite types and a fresh-legged, low-mileage runner swoops from a position it was forced into.
scenarios.body: Written In My Soul is young (6yo), lightly raced and has run exclusively on good ground — though a natural hold-up type forced slightly forward, its freshness and age could be an asset if the field is strung out. Love Like This won over 24f on good and is trained by John Patrick Ryan (same yard as Kilashee), whose runner could benefit from stable intelligence; its true hold-up style means this scenario depends on a very strong early pace genuinely punishing the leaders.

watchPoints.text: Sampoet and Kilashee will duel for the lead from the off — watch the early fractions closely because if neither concedes, the pace could be severe enough to blow the race wide open from the third-last, dramatically boosting hold-up horses like Il Silenzio.

Stormy Master and Made U Look are true hold-up horses mapped into midfield — if they get caught in traffic in the middle of the pack with 19 runners, their chance is further compromised beyond the redistribution itself; watch for traffic problems turning for home.
Deal Again returns from 637 days off — watch for any signs of ring rustiness early; a horse that fades in finishes after nearly two years off in a 19-runner 3m1f chase is a major non-completion risk.

Thewaybackhome is the only 5yo in the field tackling a 3m1f handicap chase — watch whether he settles in a prominent position through the first mile or is bustled along, as his ability to travel without exertion will be the key indicator of whether he stays the trip.

Trainer John Patrick Ryan has two runners (Kilashee, Love Like This) — watch for any market support on Love Like This as the stable's live runner; Kilashee's role as a pacemaker could be tactical cover for the yard's second string.
